headline: Highest risk is medium: CrewAI can write and execute in a shared host workspace, while Pathway is read-only/local-only, so prompt injection and leakage are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and parse tool outputs in a shared-memory crew model; Pathway is document-processing with no filesystem or network surfaces, so direct hijack from B is limited. Still, if B’s documents are fed into CrewAI as trusted content, injected instructions can steer A. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are ingested by CrewAI as instructions or tool arguments
IF CrewAI reads untrusted documents from its working directory without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate instruction and data channels in CrewAI
Prefix all Pathway text with untrusted-data markers
Disable automatic tool execution on parsed document text
Add a manual review step before CrewAI acts on Pathway output
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI can touch developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Pathway has no filesystem, network, or clipboard surfaces and no data classes listed. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound path from Pathway, so leakage risk is small and mostly limited to accidental exposure through CrewAI’s host files.
conditions: IF sensitive crew inputs are stored in CrewAI’s working directory
IF Pathway is configured to read files from the same host directory via external orchestration
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared working directory
Restrict CrewAI file access to a dedicated subfolder
Run Pathway on separate input mounts
Rotate any API keys exposed to CrewAI
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem and execute_shell, but Pathway has no write, shell, subprocess, or git capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because B is explicitly read-only/local-only.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory
IF Pathway is wrapped with additional write-capable tooling not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes from CrewAI to shared artifacts
Keep Pathway read-only
Use file locks for any shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from developer-passed data and act through tools, while Pathway is a document-processing system that could feed those outputs downstream. If Pathway consumes CrewAI results without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect documents or pipeline actions. The pathway is inferred from the profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Pathway treats CrewAI output as authoritative input
IF CrewAI-produced text is transformed into downstream records without validation
mitigations: Add schema validation on CrewAI outputs
Require human review for high-impact fields
Compare outputs against source documents
Log and reject malformed records
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while Pathway’s profile shows no data classes or residency/compliance commitments. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of compliance surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI without a matching retention policy
IF Pathway is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules than the host environment
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to CrewAI
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Document retention settings for both systems
Review vendor terms for data handling
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
